title: Collapse of a liquid column (dam break): the surge front and the column's fall against Martin and Moyce
source: J. C. Martin, W. J. Moyce, Part IV. An experimental study of the collapse of liquid columns on a rigid horizontal plane, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 244 (1952) 312–324: Table 2 (rectangular section, n² = 2, a = 2¼ in, the mean of nine records: the surge front Z = z/a against T = n t √(g/a)) and Table 6 (n² = 2, a = 2¼ in: the column's top H = h/(n² a) against τ = t √(g/a))

quantities.quantity: T(Z = 3.00) − T(Z = 1.44): the front's time from 1.44 a to 3.00 a in units of 1 / (n √(g/a))
quantities.reason: the simulated liquid is 200 times more viscous than water (the lattice holds τ ≥ 0.505 on this grid; Reynolds number about 350 on the front speed and a), which slows the front along the no-slip floor: the refinement study (README) finds the interval 18.9 % long at 25 cells per a, 12.8 % at 50 (this case) and 9.9 % at 100, the viscosity halving with each refinement at fixed τ; the nine records spread ±0.14 in T at Z = 3 (±10 % of the interval)
as the first interval: 16.2 % long at 25 cells per a, 10.2 % at 50 (this case), 6.9 % at 100; the records spread ±0.15 in T at Z = 4.11

quantities.quantity: H = h / (n² a) at the plane of symmetry at τ = 2 (frame 2), from the liquid depth in the first column of cells
quantities.reason: Table 6's time origin is the release trigger and the motion began at or before τ = 0.16, which moves H(τ = 2) by up to 0.05; the refinement study finds 0.502 at 25, 50 (this case) and 100 cells per a

quantities.quantity: H(τ = 1) − H(τ = 2): the column's fall between τ = 1 (frame 1) and τ = 2 (frame 2); Table 6 gives 0.806 at τ = 1 (between 0.83 at 0.93 and 0.78 at 1.08) and 0.50 at τ = 2
quantities.reason: a difference of two heights, which the uncertain time origin hardly moves; H(τ = 1) is interpolated between two tabulated rows (±0.01); the refinement study finds 0.303, 0.302 (this case) and 0.303 at 25, 50 and 100 cells per a
the mass exchange and the conversions are exact; round-off over the run
